findings.evidence: Lines 77–80 are the only characterization of `coordinateMap`; the required computation ultimately uses `MonoidAlgebra.mapDomain_single`, as confirmed by `DiagonalizableGroup/Functoriality.lean:122–123`.
findings.fix: Add a `@[simp]` lemma stating that `toBialgHom (coordinateMap R φ)` sends `MonoidAlgebra.single g r` (at least `single g 1`) to `single (toMonoidHom φ g) r`.
findings.issue: The coordinate-map API identifies the underlying bialgebra hom but provides no pointwise basis-element rule, so consumers must unfold Mathlib’s map-domain implementation to prove how characters transform.

findings.evidence: Lines 68–74 define both directions, while `FiniteType/CommHopfAlgCat.lean` provides the parallel `ofHom_toBialgHom` and `toBialgHom_ofHom` lemmas.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` lemmas for `toMonoidHom (ofHom φ) = φ` and `ofHom (toMonoidHom φ) = φ`.
findings.issue: The `ofHom`/`toMonoidHom` introduction-elimination API is incomplete: unlike the parallel finite-type Hopf category, it has no simp round-trip lemmas, forcing downstream users to rely on abbreviation reduction.

findings.evidence: Lines 30–37 expose the definition and immediately provide the exact public restatement, so no consumer needs unfolding.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` and keep the body opaque behind `fgCommGrpProperty_iff`.
findings.issue: `fgCommGrpProperty` exposes its body even though the public `@[simp]` theorem `fgCommGrpProperty_iff` already supplies its complete membership API.

summary: The new categorical wrappers lack key characteristic lemmas, and one implementation body is unnecessarily exposed.
